judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard consideration/reliance preamble; the only oddities are OCR corruptions, not drafting defects, and nothing operative turns on the wording.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It ties coverage to 'the statements in the declarations' and 'all the terms of this policy', which fits the Declarations and Conditions; no provision contradicts it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The grant hinges on 'ultimate net loss in excess of the retained limit', both defined elsewhere, so the phrase itself is definite though the follow-form/indemnity-only structure invites argument.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Read against Definition d (c034 Retained Limit), Condition 5 Loss Payable (c048) and the SIR reimbursement clause (c012), the point at which the umbrella attaches is not stated consistently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The trigger 'not covered by any underlying coverage ... or any other underlying insurance collectible by the insured' is workable but 'collectible' is a term with contested reach.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be read with II(a)/(b) (c008, c009), the Other Insurance condition (c052) and the Asbestos no-defence endorsement (c081), which together leave the defence obligation patchy.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A duty to defend even 'groundless, false or fraudulent' suits sits beside a discretion to settle 'as it deems expedient', a familiar tension over whether the duty is mandatory.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The asbestos endorsement (c081) expressly negates any defence duty for one class of suit, showing the base duty is qualified elsewhere but not otherwise contradicted.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Bond-premium obligations are enumerated with clear caps and an express disclaimer of any duty to furnish bonds.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Nothing in the Conditions or endorsements addresses bonds, so no conflict arises.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Costs and post-judgment interest are defined by reference to the company's limit; the language is conventional and self-limiting.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It coheres with the Appeals condition (c047) and with 'ultimate net loss' (c033), which excludes such expenses, so they are additive rather than inconsistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Reimbursement 'at the company's request' with a carve-out for loss of earnings is narrow and concrete.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the ultimate net loss definition (c033) excluding the insured's own salaries and office expenses.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One sentence disclaiming expenses 'covered by underlying insurance'; the only softness is whether 'covered by' means paid, payable or within scope.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Read with the supplementary-payments lead-in (c003) and Maintenance of Underlying Insurance (c056), where a lapsed underlying policy is deemed in force, the allocation of defence cost becomes uncertain.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The drop-down defence obligation is conditioned on being 'immediately in excess of underlying insurance listed on the declarations page without intervening insurance', which is specific but hard to apply where a self-insured retention intervenes.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Against Definition d (c034), which allows the retained limit to be the SIR, and the Loss Payable condition (c048), it is unclear when limits are 'exhausted' for this purpose.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The exception 'except settlement of claims or suits' is clumsily inserted and its effect on which payments erode the limit is not obvious.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It works with the definition of ultimate net loss (c033), which already excludes loss and legal expenses, so the two largely overlap rather than conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short savings clause for jurisdictions where the company is 'prevented by law' from defending; the trigger is broad but the consequence is plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No other provision addresses jurisdictional impediments, so nothing contradicts it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single, definite reimbursement obligation keyed to the SIR 'stated in Item 4 of the declarations'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It assumes the company pays within the SIR, whereas Loss Payable (c048) says liability does not attach until the underlying limit has been paid by the insured, and Definition d (c034) treats the SIR as an alternative retained limit.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The occurrence limit and the products/completed-operations aggregate are stated numerically by cross-reference; the only softness is 'arising out of'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: This paragraph is expressly replaced by the Aggregate Limits Endorsement (c084), which adds 'any professional liability hazard', and the declared limits ($18M occurrence/$9M aggregate) are further amended by Endorsement No. 4 (c109) to $20M/$20M.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Occurrences happening anywhere' is about as definite as a territory clause can be.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Two Policy Territory Amended endorsements (c105, c113) purport to amend territory for a 'Hospital Professional Liability coverage part' that is not part of this umbrella form, leaving the relationship unclear.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The unpunctuated string 'worker's or unemployment compensation disability benefits or similar law' leaves the catch-all 'similar law' and the reach of each listed scheme uncertain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No other provision grants employer's-liability-type coverage beyond the scheduled underlying Employers Liability policy, so there is no direct clash.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The nuclear-energy exclusion is long but keyed to named policies and statutes, leaving little to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is supported by the definitional paragraph for exclusions (b) and (c) (c018) and contradicted by nothing else.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard nuclear-material exclusion; the text is badly scanned but the enumerated triggers are conventional and specific.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Cross-refers to the definitions in c018 and is untouched by any endorsement.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Purely definitional, and the definitions are borrowed wholesale from the Atomic Energy Act.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It serves exclusions (b) and (c) (c016, c017) and nothing else touches it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The loss-of-use exclusion turns on 'level of performance, quality, fitness or durability warranted or represented' and on a 'sudden and accidental' carve-back, both contested phrases, and the text here is run together with unrelated definitions.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits against the property damage definition (c036), which expressly covers loss of use of undamaged property, so the exclusion largely takes back part of the grant.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Any other organization coming under the named insured's control of which it assumes active management' is vague at the edges: 'control' and 'active management' have no stated test.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Additional Named Insureds endorsement (c085) and Endorsements Nos. 6-8 (c115, c117, c119-c120) list entities individually and disclaim automatic coverage for newly acquired entities, which pulls against the automatic-control language here.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The insured definition for premises, executive officers and real-estate managers is conventional, though this scan is fragmentary.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It coheres with the Named Insured definition (c020) and the additional insured endorsements (c085, c088).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Omnibus automobile insured clause, truncated here but standard in form.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the scheduled Sentry automobile underlying policy and the intrafamily carve-out in the cross-suits endorsement (c061).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The follow-form opening 'except insofar as coverage is provided in the underlying insurance as scheduled herein' makes the exclusion's scope depend on another document rather than its own words.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No aircraft policy appears in the Item 7 schedule, so the carve-back may be empty; that must be read with the Schedule of Underlying Insurance.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The final qualifier 'to the extent the insured is under contract to provide insurance' narrows the care-custody-control branch in a way that is easy to dispute.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Care, Custody & Control Exclusion endorsement (c075) excludes the same property without that qualifier, so the two versions of the same exclusion are not the same width.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The sistership exclusion is enumerated and conventional; 'known or suspected defect' is the only soft phrase.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It coheres with the products hazard definition (c041) and nothing amends it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An enumerated list of four advertising offences with a proviso about 'slogans' that is garbled, leaving the carve-out's reach unclear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Advertising Liability definition (c037) affirmatively covers infringement of title or slogan, which this exclusion appears partly to withdraw.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Racing and demolition-contest exclusion; the terms are concrete and the risk is remote for a hospital.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Nothing elsewhere grants racing coverage.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The 'sudden and accidental' exception to the pollution exclusion is one of the most litigated phrases in liability insurance and is undefined here.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Total Pollution Exclusion endorsement (c093) purports to replace this exclusion, but describes the replaced wording imprecisely, so which pollution exclusion governs is itself a question.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: This watercraft/aircraft insured fragment is so garbled that its enumerated exceptions cannot be traced with confidence.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits with the aircraft exclusion (c023) and the aircraft definition (c039) without evident contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A dangling fragment ('operations by or on behalf of the named insured or to facilities of or used by the named insured') that cannot be read alone.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It belongs to the insured definition in c029 and does not conflict with anything else.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Sweeping any underlying-policy insured into this policy 'subject to all the limitations upon coverage under such policy other than the limits' invites argument about which limitations carry over.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be reconciled with the additional insured endorsement (c088), the Additional Named Insureds list (c085) and the professional services exclusion (c082), which restrict who is covered here.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The partnership/joint venture clause is conditional and internally complete.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Declarations designate the Named Insured as a Corporation, so this branch is dormant rather than conflicting.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Sum actually paid or payable in cash', 'settlement with the written consent of the company' and the exclusion of all loss and legal expenses are all points on which insureds and insurers routinely differ.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It has to be squared with supplementary payments being 'in addition to the ultimate net loss' (c010), the Appeals condition (c047) and the Overlap Endorsement (c106), which promises indemnity for legal expenses.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The 'greater of' formula combining scheduled limits, 'any other underlying insurance collectible by the insured' and the SIR is a classic source of attachment-point disputes.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It pulls against Condition 5 Loss Payable (c048), the SIR reimbursement clause (c012), Other Insurance (c052) and Maintenance of Underlying Insurance (c056), which each describe attachment differently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition bundles bodily injury with offence-type injuries and adds an exception-riddled sub-paragraph (5) on 'racial or religious discrimination not committed by or on behalf of the insured', which is awkward and hard to apply.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Personal Injury Endorsement (c058) strips out most of these heads and the Exclusion of Discrimination (c079) removes discrimination entirely, directly contradicting sub-paragraph (5).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard two-limb property damage definition; the 'occurs during the policy period' trigger is definite though it can bite in long-tail claims.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It fits the occurrence definition (c038) and the care-custody-control exclusions (c024, c075) without contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Four enumerated advertising offences, the third of which ('idea misappropriation under an implied contract') is a phrase of uncertain scope.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The advertising offence exclusion (c026) takes back parts of this grant, so the two must be read together.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Accident, including continuous or repeated exposure to conditions', 'neither expected nor intended' and the deeming of 'all such exposure to substantially the same general conditions existing at or emanating from one location or source' as one occurrence are exactly the phrases number-of-occurrences litigation turns on.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Because the per-occurrence limit (c013/c084) and the SIR in Item 4 both apply 'each occurrence', how this deeming sentence operates changes the money at stake across the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line, concrete definition of aircraft.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Used only by the aircraft exclusion (c023); no tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line, concrete definition of automobile.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the omnibus automobile insured clause (c022) and the scheduled auto policy.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition opens with 'personal injury and property damage' but then conditions on 'the bodily injury or property damage', using an undefined term inconsistently with the defined one.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The mismatch matters because the aggregate limit (c013/c084) applies only to products/completed operations hazards, and 'personal injury' is separately defined in c035 and cut down by c058.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Completed operations hazard is defined by two cumulative conditions that are workable, if fact-sensitive.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is elaborated by the Operations definition (c043) and used by the aggregate limit provisions (c013, c084) coherently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Three enumerated completion triggers plus two carve-outs; detailed and mechanical rather than open-ended.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It dovetails with the completed operations hazard definition (c042) and nothing amends it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single sentence pointing to the declarations; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Pay Plan Endorsement (c097-c098) instalments total the $29,890 shown in Item 5, so the two are consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A permissive inspection right with an express no-warranty disclaimer; clear on its face.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No other provision imposes an inspection duty or a different record-retention period.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Whenever it appears that an occurrence is likely to involve indemnity' and 'as soon as practicable' are elastic triggers that late-notice disputes are built on.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Wisconsin Amendatory Endorsement (c073) limits the effect of failed conditions to those that increase the risk or contribute to the loss, softening this condition in a way that must be harmonised.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An optional appeal right with costs additional to the limit; the mechanism is stated clearly.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It coheres with the ultimate net loss definition (c033) and the supplementary payments 'in addition' clause (c010).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Shall not attach until the amount of the underlying limit has been paid by or on behalf of the insured' is the classic exhaustion phrase, and 'by or on behalf of' is precisely where insured and insurer part company.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits uneasily with Definition d (c034), which allows the SIR alone to be the retained limit, and with Maintenance of Underlying Insurance (c056), which deems unmaintained underlying cover to be in force.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The surviving fragment barring joinder of the company is badly garbled and cannot be read as a whole sentence.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Wisconsin Amendatory Endorsement (c070) deletes the 'Action Against Company' condition 'in its entirety' and substitutes a clause entitling any person or organisation to recover, so this text is contradicted outright.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The scanned text is truncated but the rule — insolvency does not relieve the company — is standard and unambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The same rule is restated in the Wisconsin Amendatory Endorsement (c070), a duplication rather than a conflict.
